newsitem.title: JAPAN: Nissan mulls nickel battery-powered electric car.
newsitem.headline: Nissan mulls nickel battery-powered electric car.

text.p: Nissan Motor Co Ltd said on Wednesday that it is considering developing an electric vehicle powered by a nickel-metal hydride battery.
However, the company denied a newspaper report that it plans to buy the battery from a new joint venture to be set up by rival Toyota Motor Corp and Matsushita Electric Industrial Co Ltd.
Nissan Motor has been preparing to sell an electric vehicle powered by another type of battery, lithium ion, which is being developed in cooperation with Sony Corp.

Nissan plans to launch a recreational vehicle in Japan next year that will be powered by a lithium ion battery. The company plans to start marketing the car in the United States in January 1998, a company spokeswoman said.

Lithium ion batteries do not have to be recharged as often as nickel-metal hydride batteries. However, the production costs of lithium ion batteries are considerably higher than those of the rival product, the spokeswoman said.
